_comment: A brittle spear block (team 0: 72 Spearmen at morale 6, Tight) facing west is ordered at tick 14 to attack a 100-man Infantry block (team 1, Tight) 240 wu west of it (#1825, re-judged for #1949). It breaks while still in contact and flees north: each routed man runs on his own from the infantry he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), and the infantry follows in its ranks. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch: the melee breaks it at ticks 474 to 546, it is in contact at tick 540 on every seed (pinned; the pin was at tick 560, where seed 2, broken at tick 474, is already clear), ROUTING at tick 560, and ROUTING at tick 820. Seeds 0 to 3 are out of contact at ticks 700 and 740. On seed 4 they are not: the infantry, marching after the spearmen at 80 wu/s, keeps up with their centroid, which makes about 54 wu/s, and the two stay in contact from the break to the clip's end (tick 880) while the infantry cut down 4 of the 67; on seed 0 they meet again from tick 820. Faster foot keeping a slow rout in reach and cutting down its stragglers is the realistic outcome, so the out-of-contact pin at tick 740 (false, which seed 4 fails) is retired for a seed-robust one: the spearmen's centroid stands at (1087.09 to 1281.11, 950.22 to 1077.61) at tick 880, north-east of where they broke at about (967 to 992, 1208 to 1252), pinned at the span's midpoint (1184.1, 1013.9) with a tol of 98 wu reaching its farther ends; a rout that stalled at the infantry would read about (980, 1215), outside it. On main 1d0d7705 every seed was clear by tick 778. #1825 pinned grid_off_heading 124 (tol 16.3 degrees) at tick 560, the angle its slot grid stood off its heading after a snapped first flight turn, and moved its couple() anchor onto the men ahead along that heading. The bottom-up flight (#1949) removed the grid a routed man would keep and the anchor: a routed unit's position is the centroid of its men. So the grid pin is retired. The state ticks every 10 from 740 to the clip's end let the regular scan see the pursuer's deformation the exemption covers. The clip ends at tick 880.

follow_error.reason: follow_error, the relational successor of shape_residual, reads uid1 27.61 against 6.75 on this tree (dense 2-tick FULL dump, Windows, seed 0, measured 2026-11-13); the slot-based shape_residual this exemption was written against read uid1 25.7. Original reason: The infantry pursuer (uid 1) follows the router with its grid still scrambled from the fight, from the tick contact breaks (732 on this seed) to the clip's end. Dense 2-tick FULL dumps, every exemption removed, Windows, measured 2026-11-07: on main 1d0d7705 seeds 0 to 4 read 23.97, 19.56, 24.47, 26.13 and 19.17, and on the fix 580995c5 25.70, 19.70, 27.58, 24.18 and 19.65, against 6.75. On this seed on the fix it passes over ticks 2 to 700 and reads 22.40 over ticks 700 to 760, 25.61 over 760 to 820 and 25.70 over 820 to 880. It is not caused by the router's anchor: main fails the same way. Tracked as #1824, a pursuer deforming at the edge of a router's contact range.
